newsitem.title: USA: Houston annexes northeast suburb of Kingwood.
newsitem.headline: Houston annexes northeast suburb of Kingwood.

text.p: Houston's city council on Wednesday voted to annex Kingwood, a northeast suburb that fought being pulled inside the city's limits.

But Kingwood officials, who came close to negotiating a settlement that would have assured its independence, were expected to return to a federal court seeking to block the annexation, officials said.
Houston Mayor Bob Lanier, who initiated annexation proceedings, said Kingwood residents should share costs of maintaining services in one of the country's largest metropolitan areas.

"What it amounts to is, we're putting about a $4,000 to $5,000 mortgage on peoples' homes in Houston for the benefit of people that live in the county but outside the city limits, and that's wrong," Houston Mayor Bob Lanier said.

Kingwood officials had offered Houston a $5.3 million a year package of water assessment fees and road construction funds to remain outside the city limits, but eleventh-hour talks to avoid annexation broke down.
Kingwood volunteer firefighters were clearing out of three firehouses to make way for paid city firefighters, and Houston police were moving 51 officers into precinct houses there.
